results.reader_title: Forecasting emerging technologies from patents when training data is scarce
results.reader_what: Generating synthetic training samples lets deep learning forecast emerging technologies from limited labelled patent data.
results.reader_why: Removes the labelled-data bottleneck that has limited machine learning in technology forecasting.
results.reader_more: Deep learning can forecast emerging technologies from patent data but normally needs large volumes of labelled patents, which are hard to obtain. The authors propose combining data augmentation with deep learning to overcome this. They first construct a sample data set using Gartner's hype cycle together with multiple patent features. They then use a generative adversarial network, a model in which two networks compete so that one learns to produce realistic synthetic examples, to expand the data set. Finally they train a deep neural network classifier on the augmented data. The classifier predicted up to seventy-seven per cent of the emerging technologies in a given year with high precision. Applied to Gartner's 2017 hype cycles using patent data from 2000 to 2016, it forecast four of six emerging technologies correctly.

deep_analysis.main_finding: Augmenting scarce labelled patent data with synthetic samples lets a deep classifier identify emerging technologies with useful accuracy.
deep_analysis.method_or_basis: Sample construction from Gartner hype cycles and patent features, generative adversarial network augmentation, and deep neural network classification.
deep_analysis.qualification: Validated against Gartner hype cycle listings, which are themselves a proprietary judgement-based benchmark; four of six correct in the test case.
